{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Gibraltar|Cuisine of Gibraltar]]

'''Minestra''' is a typical [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Genoese]] dish, not to be confused with the [[Cookbook:Basque cuisine|Basque]] ‘menestra’ which is simply mixed boiled vegetables, or with [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] minestrone, a thick vegetable soup.

==Ingredients==
 
* 2 [[Cookbook:Zucchini|courgettes]], roughly [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Eggplant|aubergine]], roughly [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 large piece [[Cookbook:Pumpkin|pumpkin]], roughly [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], roughly [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kohlrabi|kohlrabi]] (colinabo), roughly [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnips]], roughly [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 UK pint (600 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Stock|vegetable stock]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* 1 head of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* Dried [[Cookbook:Kidney Bean|kidney beans]], [[Cookbook:Soaking|soaked]] overnight
* [[Cookbook:Pasta|Fideua]] (spaghetti)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
 
==Procedure==
# Combine the courgettes, aubergines, pumpkin, onion, and kohlrabi in a large pot or [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooking|pressure cooker]]. Add the vegetable stock and 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Bring to pressure and cook for 8–10 minutes, or [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 1 hour. Cool, then [[Cookbook:Purée|purée]] the whole thing. 
# Place a large handful of basil leaves and about 6 cloves of garlic in a [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|mortar]] and pound until roughly crushed and a gritty paste is achieved. Add to the pot, stir and season to taste.
# Meanwhile, [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] the beans separately until soft, then add to purée mixture.
# Boil the pasta until ''[[Cookbook:Al dente|al dente]]'' then add to mixture.
# Serve with [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan]] or hard Edam sprinkled over it.

== Warnings ==

* Dried kidney beans will cause nausea, vomiting and diarrhea unless they have been boiled briskly (a slow cooker is not sufficient) for at least 20 minutes to destroy the very indigestible [[W:Phytohaemagglutinin|phytohaemagglutinin]] that they contain. They will then need another 60–90 minutes at a slow simmer to be tender. Tinned kidney beans are quite safe and do not need pre-cooking as their preparation involves sufficient heat to destroy the toxin.
